misconceptions.description: Attributing a rendering bug to the browser or platform when the real cause is an unclosed or malformed tag in the learner's own HTML
misconceptions.trigger: learner sees runaway styling and concludes the browser is broken rather than inspecting their tags
misconceptions.feedback: Most layout breaks are unbalanced tags. Read the markup around the symptom and check that each element that opens also closes.

misconceptions.description: Expecting a useful debugging answer from a vague prompt like fix my site instead of stating the symptom and pasting the relevant code
misconceptions.trigger: learner asks the AI to fix it without describing the error or sharing code
misconceptions.feedback: Give the AI the symptom, the exact code block, and a specific question. A targeted prompt produces an answer you can verify against your files.

misconceptions.description: Acting on an AI diagnosis that does not fit the situation, such as a CORS fix for a same-folder local image
misconceptions.trigger: learner applies an off-target AI fix without checking whether the diagnosed cause is even possible in their context
misconceptions.feedback: Test the diagnosis against your context. If the named cause cannot apply, ignore the fix and look at the simpler explanation, usually a path or filename typo.

misconceptions.description: Committing an AI-suggested fix without reloading and confirming in the browser console that the error is actually gone
misconceptions.trigger: learner pastes a fix and commits it based on the AI's confidence alone
misconceptions.feedback: Reload and check the developer console. A cleared error message is the evidence the fix worked; the AI saying so is not.
